## What these figures mean, and what they do not

- **"Located"** means the article's start was found in the text. The headword stored in each
  row is always the index's, correctly spelled; `headword_ocr` is what the OCR printed.
- **How articles are located.** A verbatim pass places every headword it can, in printed order.
  The headwords it leaves, run by run between placed neighbours, are *aligned* in order to the
  article starts in that span (a line whose head, of about the headword's length and without
  punctuation, is followed by ( or [), at similarity ≥ 0.70. A headword broken across a line with a
  hyphen is joined. An entry printed with a spelling variant inside it, အနုပါဒိဏ္ဏ(န္န)ကဇာတိ, is one
  printed article for two index headwords: both spellings are read, and the second headword shares
  the first one's article (`variant_of`). Pages the index does not cover at all lie inside a long
  article and are read whole into it (`runs_through`).
- **How good the placements are.** Checked against the page images in vol. 1: 36 of 38 sampled
  fuzzy placements start at the right entry. Checked against the typed witness (below): the
  analysis we read agrees with the witness's as often for fuzzy placements as for verbatim ones
  (share with similarity < 0.4: 2.9% verbatim, 3.7% fuzzy). A misplaced article would
  carry another entry's analysis. Read fuzzy placements as roughly 95% right, not as proofread.
- **Unlocated**: the headword is too damaged for a 0.70 match, sits in running text, or shares
  its line with a neighbour. The article's text then stays inside its predecessor's `raw`/`body`.
- **Labels are normalised** to the printed label (`label`); `label_ocr` keeps the reading and
  `label_how` says `exact`, `mapped` or `inferred`. The map and its checks are in `docs/labels.md`.
  Readings left unnormalised (listed above the notes) are mostly digits standing for a lost label
  and spelling variants the reader did not attach to the headword.
- **Against the typed witness.** Pali Canon E-Dictionary 1.94 holds this dictionary as typed text
  (`docs/labels.md` §4). It has an entry for 6,903 of 7,189 (96.0%) of this volume's headwords. Where both have a
  label, ours agrees on 97.9% of articles, or 99.2% of those we normalised.
- **+ signs in the compound analysis are repaired** (`normalise_analysis`; the OCR text is kept in
  `analysis_ocr`). An analysis whose closing ] was misread is taken as the run of +-joined
  elements and flagged `analysis_bracket_damaged`. Its last element may keep the character the ]
  was read as (ပရိစ္ဆိန္နံ for ပရိစ္ဆိန္န]). Word formations can be cross-checked at
  https://dictionary.sutta.org/.
- **Citations** are parsed only in their full form (abbreviation ၊ vol ။ para ။). Cross-reference
  articles (`X-ကြည့်`) have none by design.
- **OSBCT**: the residual of headwords unattested is lemmata the canon never inflects that way and
  compounds formed for the entry, not romanisation failure.
- Every row is `status: "ocr"`. Nothing is proofread.

## Vol. 2 specifics

- **PDF pp. 241 and 242 are bound in the wrong order.** Their running heads print pages
  ၂၂၄ (224) and 223, and each carries the other's index headwords. `PAGE_FIX` in
  `abhidhana_articles.py` reads them in the right order. The OCR report's recall for those two
  pages (0 of 15) is scored against the uncorrected index.
- **Spelling-variant entries are common here.** 20 index headwords share an article with their
  variant twin. P. 115 is a page of seven such entries (အနုပါဒိဏ္ဏ(န္န)က…) for fourteen headwords.

## Spot checks against the page images

Three pages, every article compared with `02.pdf`.

| page | chosen because | index headwords | at the right entry | wrong entry | unlocated | labels |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 500 | an ordinary page | 11 | 11 | 0 | 0 | 11 right |
| 241–242 | scored 0 recall (the swapped pair) | 15 | 15 | 0 | 0 | 13 right, 2 not read |
| 115 | the weakest remaining page (4 of 14 read) | 14 | 7 | 1 | 6 | 4 right, 3 not read |

- **P. 500**: debris had broken the analysis across lines in 4 of the 11 articles. It is now read
  whole, though on 4 articles the closing ] was misread (`analysis_bracket_damaged`). The bodies
  carry the usual debris of dots and specks.
- **Pp. 241–242**, after `PAGE_FIX`: all 15 are at their own entry. The variant pair
  အနုသာ(ဿာ)ဝေတ shares one article. One start, အနုသာရီ, is placed three lines into its own article,
  because the OCR broke its first line. The labels of အနုသာရီ and အနုသာသက were not read: the
  bracket was lost.
- **P. 115**: the seven printed entries are each for a pair of spellings (fourteen index
  headwords). Seven headwords are at the right entry. The first is placed on the running head,
  which carries the variant and debris, and is therefore wrong. Six are unlocated: the OCR broke the
  heads of those entries past a 0.70 match. This is the worst case, not the typical one.

## Re-run, 25 September 2026

`abhidhana_articles.py` now reads a homonym's superscript numeral, which OCR turns into debris
glued to the headword (အါ, အဝ်, အည”, အမူလကာါ), and places a one- or two-character headword on a
line of its own. The pass runs last, only for headwords still unplaced and only inside the span
their placed neighbours leave, so no earlier placement moved. 6,723 → 6,724 located (+1): a homonym whose superscript was read as ”. The tables above are
the re-run's.

**Labels with a lost bracket** (25 September 2026, later): a label whose ( or ) was lost, with the
[ of the analysis after it — "(ကြို [", "ထီ) [" — is now read when the reading is one the label map
knows (`label_bracket_damaged`). 91 labels gained; label + body 87.1% → 88.4%. Checked against the
typed witness (`docs/witness.md`): 87 of the 91 it has agree, against 99% for the other labels.
No label already read changed.
